title: Review: convergence check round 6
notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — two real correctness bugs (P1): sign/verify ECDSA-SHA512 asymmetry breaks P-521 key callers silently; trust anchor pathLen enforcement gap allows cert chains RFC 5280 would reject. Plus one dead error variant that will mislead future contributors.
Confidence: 88% chance of no missed bugs. Least confident flags: (1) the pathLen intermediate-CA-in-bag check — logic is subtle and my trace-through might miss a case; (2) EccCmsSharedInfo entity_u_info handling — UKM is encoded as None in encrypt() which means UKM-aware senders cannot interoperate, but this is documented behavior not a bug. Uncertainty driven by: manual trace rather than test coverage for pathLen edge cases; no test exercising the P-521 / ECDSA-SHA512 path at all. Would raise confidence if: pathLen enforcement had a test with a constrained CA cert, and if the ECDSA-SHA512 path had even a synthetic test vector.
Idiom rating: CLEAN — no unwrap/expect outside justified locations (base64 str conversion with clear comments), no borrow-checker clone escapes, no to_string() on literals, no bare return statements. Error handling is consistent. The only idiom issue is the dead SignatureVerification variant, filed as P1.
